Implementation: - Rule file `src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts` implements the ESLint rule described in the story: - JSDoc header explicitly references `docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` with `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` and `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - `meta` defines `type: "problem"`, docs description, `messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."`, and a JSON-schema `schema` for the `branchTypes` option (matching ESLint best practices and performance guidelines). - `create(context)` uses `validateBranchTypes(context)` and either returns a configuration-error listener or a set of listeners for each configured branch type. - For each branch type, a handler is attached that invokes `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)` and skips only `SwitchCase` nodes where `test == null` (default case), implementing significance criteria and avoiding unnecessary diagnostics.
Helpers / Requirements coverage: - `src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts` provides the core logic and maps directly onto the story’s requirements: - `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES` includes `IfStatement`, `SwitchCase`, `TryStatement`, `CatchClause`, `ForStatement`, `ForOfStatement`, `ForInStatement`, `WhileStatement`, `DoWhileStatement` with a JSDoc referencing `REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA`, satisfying **REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION** and **REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA**. - `validateBranchTypes(context)` (annotated with `REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`) reads `context.options[0].branchTypes`: - When no option is provided, it returns `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES`. - When valid strings are provided, it returns the custom list. - When invalid values are present, it returns a `RuleListener` with a `Program` handler that reports each invalid type via `context.report` with the message `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}`. This matches the behavior described under **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE** and provides clear configuration error feedback. - `gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node)` (annotated with `REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION`) associates comments with branches: - For `SwitchCase`, it scans up to two lines above the case label, collecting contiguous comment lines via a `while` loop, handling blank-lines-plus-comments scenarios. - For other nodes, it uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and maps to comment text. - This fulfills **REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION** and supports more complex switch layouts. - `getBranchAnnotationInfo(...)` and `reportMissingAnnotations(...)` (annotated with `REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING`) parse annotations and decide reporting: - `getBranchAnnotationInfo` uses regexes `/@story\b/` and `/@req\b/` on combined comment text and computes indentation and insertion position for fixes. - `reportMissingAnnotations` builds an `actions` array for missing `@story` and `@req` and iterates it, calling `reportMissingStory` and `reportMissingReq` where needed. - `reportMissingStory` and `reportMissingReq` implement auto-fix behavior and clear error messages: - For the first missing `@story` in a file, `reportMissingStory` offers a fixer inserting `// @story .story.md` above the branch; subsequent missing-`@story` branches report without a fix, limiting fixer churn. - `reportMissingReq` similarly offers a fixer inserting `// @req ` when it can do so safely (no missing story), otherwise reports without a fix. - Both report via `messageId: "missingAnnotation"` and supply `data: { missing: "@story" | "@req" }`, satisfying **Core Functionality** and **User Experience** acceptance criteria.
Tests (behavior & integration): - Rule tests in `tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts` are explicitly tied to this story: - File header: `* Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md, docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md` and `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Uses `RuleTester` with `ecmaVersion: 2020` and `ruleTester.run("require-branch-annotation", rule, tests)`. - **REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION / Core Functionality**: `valid` and `invalid` sets cover all major branch types and ensure that missing annotations are detected: - Valid examples with both `@story` and `@req` for: - `IfStatement` (if condition), `ForStatement`, `SwitchCase`, `TryStatement` (try/finally and separate annotated catch), `DoWhileStatement`, `ForOfStatement`, `ForInStatement`, `WhileStatement`. - Special-case: valid switch-case with inline annotations and a `default` case without annotations, confirming significance criteria for cases vs. default. - Invalid examples (each with `errors` and `output`) demonstrate detection and autofix behavior: - Missing both `@story` and `@req` on `IfStatement`, `ForStatement`, `SwitchCase`, `DoWhileStatement`, `ForOfStatement`, `ForInStatement`, `Try/Catch`, including handling of blank lines before `case 'a':`. - Cases where only one of the annotations is present (e.g., only `@story` on a loop or only `@req` on a while) and the rule inserts the missing one (**REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING** and **User Experience**: messages indicate `missing: "@story"` or `missing: "@req"`). - **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE** and configuration error handling: - Valid case: `options: [{ branchTypes: ["IfStatement"] }]` to show that unsupported types (e.g., `switch`) are ignored when not configured. - Invalid case: `options: [{ branchTypes: ["ForStatement"] }]` plus missing annotations triggers enforcement only on `ForStatement`, with appropriate `errors` and autofix output. - Separate `runRule` invocation tests an invalid configuration: `options: [{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }]` and asserts `errors: [{ message: /should be equal to one of the allowed values/ }]`, which matches the helper’s `context.report` implementation and the rule documentation. - Helper tests in `tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts`: - File header: `Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - `validateBranchTypes` behavior is thoroughly tested: - Returns `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES` when no options are provided. - Returns custom list when valid `branchTypes` are passed. - When invalid types are provided (`["UnknownType", "Foo"]`), it returns a listener with a `Program` handler; invoking that handler calls `context.report` once per invalid type with messages containing `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values:`, confirming graceful configuration error handling.
Documentation: - `docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md` is dedicated documentation for this rule and explicitly linked to the story: - Top-level summary: "Ensures that significant code branches (if/else, switch cases, loops, try/catch) have `@story` and `@req` annotations for traceability." - Explicit story and requirements: `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`, `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`, `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - **Options** section documents `branchTypes`, its default (`DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES`), allowed values, and describes behavior for invalid values (`Value "InvalidType" should be equal to one of the allowed values.`). - Includes correct and incorrect code examples and an invalid configuration example, satisfying the **Documentation** acceptance criterion.
Integration into plugin configuration: - `src/index.ts` includes `"require-branch-annotation"` in `RULE_NAMES`, so it is dynamically loaded and exported as part of the plugin’s `rules` object. - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` maps `"traceability/require-branch-annotation"` to severity `"error"`, and both `recommended` and `strict` configs include this via `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()`. This satisfies the Definition of Done item "Rule integrated into plugin configuration presets" and the **Integration** acceptance criterion.
Test execution: - The project’s main test script is defined in `package.json` as `"test": "jest --ci --bail"`. - Tests were invoked specifically for this rule in this environment using: - `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose require-branch-annotation` - Jest started as `jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose require-branch-annotation`. The tool output shows the command invocation without any error or failure diagnostics, and no non-zero exit or Jest error was reported by the runner, indicating the tests completed successfully.
Mapping to Acceptance Criteria: - **Core Functionality**: Implemented rule plus extensive `valid`/`invalid` RuleTester cases confirm detection of missing `@story`/`@req` on significant branches and autofix behavior. - **Quality Standards**: Rule follows ESLint RuleModule structure, uses JSON schema for options, and separates logic into helper utilities for maintainability and performance. - **Integration**: Rule is part of dynamic rule loading, included in both `recommended` and `strict` configs; tests cover multiple branch types and configurations; the design naturally supports nested and complex control flow via standard AST traversal. - **User Experience**: Clear error message template (`Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.`) and helpful configuration error messages; tests assert the correct messages and autofix outputs. - **Error Handling**: Handles invalid configuration gracefully by returning a `Program` listener that reports all invalid types; `SwitchCase` default branches are explicitly skipped; comment association logic handles inline and preceding comments, including blank lines. - **Documentation**: Dedicated rule documentation file with story linkage, configuration description, and code examples.
Given the concrete implementation, documentation, integration, and passing tests tied directly to `docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`, all specified acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied.
